item.title: Over 1,000 free health checks mark World Diabetes Day in Valletta
item.description: More than 1,000 free health checks were carried out at Parliament Square in Valletta on Saturday to mark World Diabetes Day, with passers-by offered blood sugar level tests, blood pressure checks, dietary advice and foot health consultations. The event was organised by the Malta Medical Students' Association in collaboration with HealthMark, bringing students and healthcare professionals into the community. HealthMark CEO Charlotte Sant Portanier said the aim was to make it easier for people to ask questions and take the next step where support is needed, while MMSA public health officer Kristina Sammut said the initiative lets students apply what they learn in practice.

item.title: Multigas announces €4 million investment as it marks a century in business
item.description: Industrial gas supplier Multigas announced a €4 million investment as it marked 100 years in business, with the money going to expand the company's nitrogen production capacity. The investment was unveiled at an event at Trident Park in Mrieħel on Friday. CEO Noel Micallef said the company also plans to upgrade its administrative facilities in Kirkop and invest in automation, advanced process controls and digital technology. Multigas traces its origins to 1926, when L. Farrugia & Sons began producing carbon dioxide in Ħamrun, expanding into oxygen, nitrogen and acetylene before relocating its main operations to Kirkop in 2002. The company obtained authorisation to produce medicinal oxygen locally in 2005 and supplies gases used by industry, pharmaceutical manufacturers and healthcare providers, including medicinal oxygen for hospitals and home patients.

item.title: Police fraud warning over messages claiming unpaid traffic fines
item.description: The Malta Police Force has warned the public about fraudulent messages sent from foreign numbers claiming to be unpaid traffic fines, offering a 30% discount if the recipient pays within seven days through a link in the message. Police said the messages detail an alleged infraction, its consequences and legal implications, and are part of a scam. The authority asked recipients not to click the links or provide personal or banking details, which could be used to steal information, access accounts or spread the scam, and advised verifying any such claim directly with the relevant organisation through another means of communication. Police also recommended deleting the messages and cautioned against clicking suspicious links even when they appear to come from someone known.

item.title: Farrugia called MPs 'clowns': Labour MP seeks Speaker's ruling on alleged breach of privilege
item.description: Labour MP Nigel Vella asked the Speaker for a ruling on Monday over an alleged breach of parliamentary privilege after Malta Employers' Association director general Joseph Farrugia called him and Neville Gafa clowns in a Facebook post. Vella presented copies of the post in parliament ahead of a debate, arguing the remarks constitute a breach of privilege. The dispute follows Farrugia's decision to return his Ġieħ ir-Repubblika honour in protest against the verdict in the Yorgen Fenech case. Separately, the association said it was correcting a misrepresentation in some media after a parliamentary question by Vella reported that Farrugia earns some €20,000 a year from sitting on government boards, amounts the association said were wrongly inflated.

item.title: Student charged with grievously injuring man in Paceville nightclub fight
item.description: A 20-year-old British dental student was charged on Monday with grievously injuring another man in a fight outside Havana club in Paceville in the early hours of Sunday. Saad Adam Khan Raja, of Liverpool, appeared before Magistrate Ingrid Bianco with a bandaged hand and pleaded not guilty to grievous bodily harm and to attempting to use force with intent to insult, annoy or hurt. Police said they were called to a fight outside Footlose club on St George's Road at around 1am and found one man with injuries around the mouth and another with an injured hand, with the victim's injuries certified as grievous. Inspector Nigel Buhagiar led the prosecution and no request for bail was made.

item.title: Bishop calls for greater responsibility on road safety at Mass for traffic accident victims
item.description: Auxiliary Bishop Joseph Galea-Curmi called on the public to take greater responsibility for road safety while officiating at a Mass in memory of traffic accident victims, organised for the first time by Doctors for Road Safety at the Mater Dei Hospital chapel. Relatives and friends of victims of road accidents in Malta attended the concelebrated Mass with Fr Frankie Cini. In his homily the bishop drew on the Sunday Gospel's parable of the talents, describing life as the greatest talent entrusted to humanity, and said those behind the wheel carry responsibility not only for their own lives but for those travelling with them. Newsbook reported the bishop's remark that life is a gift from God and not our property.

item.title: Defence asks court to strike out expert evidence in Vitals hospitals concession case
item.description: The defence for three senior civil servants accused over the Vitals hospitals concession asked the court on Monday to strike out evidence produced by two inquiry experts. Lawyer Stefano Filletti challenged Miroslava Milenovic's professional qualifications and alleged conflict of interest, and accused Jeremy Harbinson of deliberately avoiding testifying in court. Former permanent secretaries Alfred Camilleri and Joseph Rapa and current permanent secretary Ronald Mizzi face charges including fraud, misappropriation of public funds and making fraudulent gains in connection with the hospitals concession, and all three have pleaded not guilty. The three were initially arraigned with former ministers Chris Fearne and Edward Scicluna in May 2024, after which the court split the case into six separate proceedings.

item.title: Government consults 46 NGOs on two bills targeting gender-based and domestic violence
item.description: The Ministry for Equality and Civil Rights consulted 46 non-governmental organisations on two bills aimed at strengthening protection for victims of domestic violence and violence against women, as part of transposing EU Directive 2024/1385 into Maltese law. The proposals cover sexual violence, technology-facilitated abuse, the sharing of intimate material without consent and stronger protection for children affected by domestic violence. The consultation meeting was organised by the Commission on Gender-Based Violence and Domestic Violence. Equality Minister Rosianne Cutajar said transposition is more than a simple legislative obligation but an opportunity to strengthen protection systems and address the challenges victims face.

item.title: PN says infrastructure investment per capita is barely keeping up with population growth
item.description: The Nationalist Party said on Monday that infrastructure investment per capita is barely changing despite population growth and worsening traffic congestion, citing a Malta Fiscal Advisory Council report. The party said that between 2019 and 2025 investment in tangible public assets per person grew by an average of just 0.3% a year once inflation and population growth are taken into account. The PN argued this points to a more fundamental problem with the government's economic model, which bases growth on population growth and demand without ensuring infrastructure and public services expand at the same pace, and said spending more money alone is not enough unless it is of high quality, delivered on time and addresses real problems. Malta Independent reported the PN also cited NSO figures showing an increase of around 50 cars a day.

item.title: Police road check: driver charged with drugs and weapons after passenger swallows suspected narcotics
item.description: A 42-year-old Albanian man was charged on Monday with possession of cocaine, a knuckleduster and an unlicensed flick knife, violently resisting arrest, disobeying police orders, driving without a seat belt and disturbing public peace, after he and his passenger were stopped during a routine road check in St Paul's Bay on 15 November. Police said the passenger resisted arrest and swallowed a suspected drug during the struggle before being taken to Mater Dei Hospital, where he was certified as being in danger of losing his life; the driver then fled and was arrested shortly afterwards, and bail was refused by Magistrate Ingrid Bianco. Reports differ on the passenger's condition: Newsbook states the passenger died at Mater Dei Hospital, while Times of Malta reports he remains certified in danger of losing his life, with his condition unchanged as of Monday.

item.title: Terrorism accused urged acquaintances to watch ISIS propaganda and travel to Syria
item.description: A 21-year-old man accused of terrorism-related offences pressured acquaintances to watch ISIS propaganda and encouraged them to travel with him to Syria, a court heard on Monday. Inspector Mohammed Shurrab of the police Counter-Terrorism Squad testified that the accused, Daniel Spiteri, spoke of killing same-sex couples and adopted increasingly extremist views following his conversion to Islam. Spiteri is pleading not guilty to charges of allegedly planning a terrorist attack, recruiting or inciting others to commit terrorist acts, and training or instructing individuals in the use of firearms for terrorist purposes. Shurrab said the squad received intelligence in May 2026 that a person known as Souleymane had travelled to Syria to join ISIS, and that police identified him and monitored his movements between May and October before arresting him on 27 October.

item.title: Scope Ratings affirms Malta's A+ long-term credit rating with stable outlook
item.description: Scope Ratings has reaffirmed Malta's long-term local and foreign currency issuer ratings at A+ with a stable outlook, following a monitoring review, while maintaining the short-term issuer rating at S-1+. The Berlin-based agency said the ratings were supported by robust economic momentum and strong growth prospects compared with other European countries, a strong record of fiscal prudence, declining budget deficits and moderate government debt, as well as a strong external position and banking sector able to absorb economic shocks. Scope did however highlight Malta's dependence on external markets and its limited resources, which it said pose risks to the sustainability of the country's economic growth model.

item.title: Man critically ill after swallowing suspected drugs during police road check
item.description: A 40-year-old Albanian man is in a life-threatening condition after he swallowed a substance suspected to be drugs while resisting arrest during a routine police road check in Triq il-Ħalel, St Pauls Bay, on Sunday morning. Officers stopped the vehicle after noticing that the driver and passenger were not wearing seatbelts, and found a knuckle duster, a substantial quantity of suspected cocaine and two knives in their possession. The passenger resisted arrest and attempted to flee, swallowing the suspected drug in the process, and was certified at Mater Dei Hospital as being in danger of losing his life. The 42-year-old driver also attempted to escape but was arrested and remains in police custody, while a police sergeant sustained slight injuries during the struggle and received treatment at a health centre.

item.title: Man arrested after assaulting his elderly parents in Birkirkara
item.description: A man was arrested and remanded after being charged with harming, insulting and causing grievous injury to his parents, aged 79 and 80, with whom he lives in Birkirkara. The court heard that between 14 and 31 October he allegedly punched his mother in the face and bruised her, and that he previously attacked his father after hearing his wife speak. He admitted the allegations but said he could not remember why he did it. Defence counsel asked for an assessment of his mental state, and Magistrate Tanya Sammut ordered psychiatric care and a possible transfer to the hospital forensic section.

item.title: Suspended sentence for thefts from elderly homes
item.description: Riccardo Conoscenti, 26, an Italian national, received a one-year suspended sentence, deferred by two years, after admitting to stealing items worth around 170 from homes for the elderly in Birkirkara and Tign, captured on CCTV. He told the court he took the objects because he believed they were worth more than they were, and apologised, saying he wished to pay for them. Magistrate Tanya Sammut also ordered him to pay for the stolen goods.

item.title: Call for cybersecurity to become part of the Maltese school curriculum
item.description: Cybersecurity education should be integrated across subjects in Maltese schools so children and teenagers are better prepared for the risks of the digital world, was a key message from a workshop held in Malta as part of the Erasmus+ EnCycLEd project. The project, coordinated by the University of Innsbruck and implemented locally by AscendConsulting.EU, has built a free educational platform for teachers, educators and career-guidance professionals and targets students aged 10 to 18. Participants stressed that the subject should be taught through practical activities tied to students daily experience, not only as a technical topic.

item.title: Conference on threats to democracy and education in a digital world
item.description: An international conference on threats to democracy and education in a digital world will be held on 26 November from 9am to 1pm at Antoine De Paule Hall, San Anton Palace, Attard, aimed at educators and officials working in diplomacy and international affairs. Speakers include former Estonian president Toomas Hendrik Ilves, Alex Meija of the United Nations Institute for Training and Research and Francesco Capp of Gioya HEI. It is organised by Maltas non-resident ambassador to Estonia and Finland Kenneth Vella with Gioya HEI, under the patronage of President Myriam Spiteri Debono, with free entry against a 10 donation to the Malta Community Chest Fund.

item.title: Harley-Davidson convoy delivers the Bora ta San Martin to children
item.description: A convoy of 60 Harley-Davidson motorcycles toured several localities to deliver the Bora ta San Martin, a boat loaded with treats and toys, to children at five centres, in an annual initiative organised by the H.O.G. Malta Chapter. Members rode with officials from Transport Malta, which provided the escort and motorcycle for the run, on a route spanning centres from Santa Venera to urrieq. The organisers said their greatest satisfaction was seeing the smiles on the childrens faces, and thanked Transport Malta, sponsors and volunteers.

item.title: Gozo marks the 1798 uprising with historical re-enactment
item.description: A historical re-enactment commemorating the uprising of the Gozitan people against French occupation forces was held in Victoria, organised by the Historical Group Re-enactment of Malta with the Circolo Gozitano and the Gozo Ministry. The event formed part of the Gozo Day celebrations marking the 28 October anniversary of the French garrisons capitulation in Gozo. The uprising was spearheaded by Archpriest Saver Cassar, who afterwards headed Gozos provisional government during 22 months of self-government.

item.title: Funding for band club music education to double to €5,000 in 2027
item.description: Funding for music education in band clubs will double from €2,500 to €5,000 per organisation in 2027, while grants for voluntary organisations working with youths will rise from €3,000 to €3,500. Youth Minister Omar Farrugia made the announcement during a conference attended by groups benefiting from the Musical Tuition for Youths in Band Clubs and BOOST schemes, both administered by Aġenzija Żgħażagħ. As part of Budget 2027 the Ministry for Youth is allocating almost €3 million for initiatives, programmes, discussions and consultations involving young people. Farrugia said 57 band clubs and band organisations qualified for assistance under the music education scheme this year, while around 130 youth organisations received support through BOOST.

item.title: Almost half of non-EU workers doubt they will still be in Malta in two years
item.description: Almost half of non-EU residents say they are unlikely to still be living in Malta in two years as new budget measures targeting foreign workers provoke opposition. A survey of 122 third-country nationals, most of whom do not hold long-term residency, found that 46% believe it unlikely they will still be in Malta in two years, compared with 7% of Maltese, while a further 20% were unsure. The same study found the controversial measures against third-country nationals, including the withdrawal of free travel and childcare services for those without long-term residency, are strongly unpopular among non-EU workers.

item.title: University students to join international youth strike on Friday
item.description: Students at the University of Malta will walk out of lectures on Friday as part of an International Youth Strike coordinated across 25 European countries, with the action taking place at noon in the university quadrangle. Organisers of the local collective say they are protesting a future compromised by what they describe as incompetent and corrupt leadership, while also raising concerns about measures affecting third-country nationals, the use of artificial intelligence and the environment. The local drive was organised by 20-year-old psychology and theatre studies student Johanke Nefe after learning about the international strike online. From rising living costs to political corruption and fears about the future, young Europeans have been taking their frustrations to the streets.

item.title: MCCAA staff get 3.5% annual salary rises to 2030 under new collective agreement
item.description: Employees of the Malta Competition and Consumer Affairs Authority will receive annual salary increases of 3.5% until 2030, alongside improved allowances, more flexible working arrangements and enhanced leave entitlements, following the signing of a new collective agreement. The 2026-2030 deal, covering staff represented by the General Workers' Union and UĦM - Voice of the Workers, introduces an immediate salary adjustment this year followed by the annual increases in basic salary scales, a new authority-wide allowance, and an enhanced qualification allowance extended to employees holding MQF Level 7 or higher qualifications. It also sets out alternative work schedules, clearly defined core working hours and improved leave provisions aimed at supporting work-life balance.

item.title: 3,843 people reported domestic violence or used support services in 2025
item.description: A total of 3,843 people in Malta reported experiencing domestic violence or used support services in 2025, according to National Statistics Office figures published on Monday, with women making up 74% of service users and men 26%. Some 55.4% used a service only once, 23.8% used one or more services twice and 20.8% used services on three or more occasions; 45.9% of women and 40.9% of men accessed services more than once. The NSO recorded 6,946 cases in total, more than the number of individuals because the same person may be counted by several providers. The Domestic Violence Unit within Aġenzija Appoġġ handled 2,913 cases and the Malta Police Force received 2,357 reports, while 622 people used services aimed at perpetrators, 93.1% of them male. item.title: EUDA survey finds Malta ranks highest in Europe on drug-related violence
item.description: Malta's drug-related violence is the country's biggest public security concern, according to the first survey by the European Union Agency for Drugs (EUDA), making Malta one of five EU countries where such violence tops the security agenda. The results draw on interviews with 95,883 people aged 15 or over across 35 European countries, using the Flash Eurobarometer methodology, and illustrate how Europeans view drugs, their impact and how society is adjusting to them.

item.title: EU tax commissioner to fly to Malta as country remains sole holdout on tobacco tax
item.description: EU taxation commissioner Wopke Hoekstra will travel to Malta on December 3 for a two-day visit, during which he is expected to discuss the EU's proposed Tobacco Taxation Directive with the Maltese government. Malta is the only one of the bloc's 27 member states still objecting to the overhaul after Finance Minister Clyde Caruana was the sole minister to vote against it at a recent EU Council meeting. Estonia and Finland, which had also objected, reversed their position after the EU dropped automatic inflation-linked increases in nicotine prices, which now require unanimity. A Commission spokesperson said the visit had been planned for some time and that the commissioner would also raise climate and taxation files including the Emissions Trading System, maritime, cars, the post-2030 framework and tax simplification.

item.title: Two women hospitalised after separate motorcycle crashes in Marsa and San Ġwann
item.description: Two women were hospitalised following separate motorcycle accidents in San Ġwann and Marsa on Monday morning. In the San Ġwann case a Chaoya motorcycle ridden by a 37-year-old Colombian woman collided with a parked Mazda in Triq San Ġiljan when the car's driver had opened the door; a 35-year-old woman from Ħaż-Żebbuġ was inside the parked vehicle. The rider was taken to Mater Dei Hospital by ambulance and was not in a critical condition. Police were then informed of a second collision in Triq it-Tiġrija, Marsa, involving a van driven by a 34-year-old man from Fgura and a Honda 125 motorcycle ridden by a 43-year-old Colombian woman from Mosta, who was also taken to hospital with her condition yet to be confirmed. The two publications differ on the order in which the accidents occurred.

item.title: Malta International Airport restructures senior leadership as traffic role changes
item.description: Malta International Airport has announced that Tina Lombardi will take on responsibility for the Traffic Development Department alongside her existing role as Senior Vice President for Commercial Development and Strategy. The expanded remit follows the departure of Alex Cardona, Senior Vice President for Traffic Development, Customer Services and Administration, who leaves after 13 years with the company. Lombardi joined MIA in 2007 and has held a senior vice president role since 2023. The airport also confirmed two appointments, with Kristian Sultana joining as MET Office Manager and Alina Alboaei named Aerodrome Safety and Compliance Manager. The changes come on the back of nine-month results showing revenue of €136.5 million, up just over 15 per cent on 14.5 per cent passenger growth, and a net profit of €50.6 million. October traffic reached 1,049,778 passengers with seat occupancy at 84.7 per cent.

item.title: Abela says European counterparts were 'stunned' by Malta's economic measures and fuel prices
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela said his European counterparts were left stunned after he explained Malta's latest Budget measures during a visit to Dublin. In an interview with Lovin Malta, Malta Daily and WhosWho.mt, Abela said colleagues started making the sign of the cross when he described the measures introduced in the Budget, particularly Malta's fuel and electricity prices and the financial support provided to households. He defended the government's economic model, saying it continues to deliver results that set Malta apart from the rest of Europe and has given the country the strongest economy in Europe. The interview follows a day in which the Nationalist Party accused the government of failing to keep infrastructure investment per capita in line with population growth.

item.title: MCAST AI project helps NGO Żibel map coastal waste from the air
item.description: A new pilot project is teaching an AI system to recognise marine litter automatically, giving the environmental NGO Żibel Malta a faster, safer way to decide where coastal clean-ups are most needed and where it is safe to send volunteers. The ICARUS system combines drone photography with machine vision and machine learning to locate and categorise coastal waste, with MCAST building the AI component. A DJI Mavic 3M drone was flown over more than a dozen Maltese coastal and inland sites, capturing over 1,000 high-resolution photographs in which individual pieces of debris, from plastic bottles and jerry cans to rubber tyres, rope and wood, were identified. Standard manual litter surveys have been slow to repeat, particularly on rocky, cliff or sub-tidal stretches of coastline.

item.title: Police seek public help to locate missing 45-year-old Sarah Desira
item.description: Police are appealing to the public for assistance in locating 45-year-old Sarah Desira, who has been reported missing. In a statement, the Malta Police Force confirmed she has been reported missing and urged anyone who may have information about her whereabouts to come forward. Information can be passed on by calling Police Headquarters on 2122 4001 or 119, or by visiting the nearest police station, and may also be given anonymously or confidentially.

item.title: Court confiscates over €13,500 from pensioner who died facing money laundering charges
item.description: A court has ordered the confiscation of more than €13,500 held in two bank accounts belonging to a Qormi pensioner who died while facing money laundering charges. Lucy Grima was accused in 2022 of usury, money laundering and offering unlicensed banking services after investigators found tens of thousands of euros in unexplained cash deposits in her accounts, prompting questions about the source of the money given that she was an unemployed pensioner. Police searching her home found handwritten ledgers recording loans she had made and the amounts borrowers were expected to repay, and several people confirmed borrowing money from her.

item.title: Road safety bureau still not set up four years after government promise
item.description: Four years after the government promised to establish a special bureau to investigate fatal road accidents and help prevent further deaths, the plan has still not got off the ground. The transport authorities say the hold-up is that they are still waiting for feedback from key stakeholders including the judiciary. The proposed Transport Safety Investigation Commission has undergone consultations with relevant stakeholders on legal and procedural considerations, but campaigners say the delay comes despite repeated warnings. Road deaths have remained at 18 last year, after 12 in 2024 and 16 in 2023, according to the National Statistics Office.

item.title: Care home applications since 2023 spark overdevelopment fears
item.description: Plans for a string of large care homes for the elderly across Malta are sparking a backlash, with residents fearing the country's ageing population will come at the expense of its shrinking countryside. Eleven applications for new or expanded care homes have been submitted in nine localities since 2023, four of them on land outside development zones. In Żejtun, developers want to replace a disused livestock farm with a three-storey care home, while an eight-storey complex able to accommodate 362 elderly residents could rise in place of an existing house in Mosta. Both proposals have drawn opposition, with residents warning the developments could damage their neighbourhood and pile further pressure on roads and infrastructure.

item.title: Teenagers drawn into TikTok weight-loss adviser rabbit holes
item.description: A teenagers worry about their body can become a rabbit hole of fear, restriction and obsessive eating on TikTok, where replies under videos invite users to post their own figures and advise strangers on what to eat or change. The report follows Dar Kenn Għal Saħħtek staff working offline with young people affected, and notes the European Commissions preliminary finding that the For You feed can repeatedly push content on body image, mental health and isolation even where it may worsen distress. Psychiatrist Anton Grech, who treats eating disorders, said the clinical picture is a group of reasons rather than one, including the influence of the media.
